ideas.title: I Fixed the Darvas Box: 74.2% Win Rate Over 33 Years
ideas.name: Mechanical Darvas box breakout on SPY (12-day high, capped chase, volume filter)
ideas.entry: Signal day: close is above the highest high of the previous 12 trading days, but by no more than 0.75% of that level, and volume is above its 15-day average (whether the average includes the signal day is unstated). Buy at the next open.
ideas.exit: When the close is above the previous day's high, sell at the next open. No stop mentioned.
ideas.filters: none by design (the video says it uses no RSI, no 200-day average, no seasonality)
ideas.claimed_results: SPY 1993 to 2026 (33 years). 279 trades, 74.2% winners, average trade +0.34%, profit factor 3.08, average hold about 3 trading days. Profit factor by era: 2.70 (1993-2004), 2.78 (2005-2015), 3.94 (2016-2026). Lookback sweep profit factors: 11d 2.75, 13d 2.97, 16d 2.84, 18d 2.71, 20d 2.80; 12d is the best at 3.08. Costs not mentioned. My arithmetic, not stated: 279 trades x 3 days over about 8,300 sessions is roughly 10% exposure.
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: none. It is a breakout, unlike everything tested so far. It shares the close-above-yesterday's-high exit with the RSI(2) sweep.
ideas.red_flags: The 0.75% chase cap and 15-day volume filter look tuned and were not swept; only the lookback was. No null comparison (same exit from random entries, or a plain 12-day-high entry without the extras). That exit lifts win rate and profit factor structurally because losers have no stop. Costs not shown. Sits oddly beside this channel's own finding that 252-day-high closes underperform over 20 days (A-32); horizon and exit differ. Promotional framing in the title.
ideas.why_priority: Complete rules, free daily data, a checkable trade count and profit factor, and the only genuinely different entry type in the folder.

ideas.title: Which Nasdaq Stocks Work Best With Williams %R? We Tested 100
ideas.name: Williams %R(2) oversold dip-buy across 101 Nasdaq-100 stocks
ideas.entry: Williams %R with a 2-day lookback closes below -90. Buy at the signal close (headline test) or at the next open (variant).
ideas.exit: Close above the prior day's high, or Williams %R rises above -30, whichever comes first.
ideas.claimed_results: Test period unstated. 95 of 101 stocks had profit factor above 1; 58 above 1.5; 26 above 2. Median profit factor 1.57 at the close, 1.47 at the next open; only 23 stocks improved with next-open entry. Apple first: 165 trades, 72.1% winners, average trade +1.19%, profit factor 3.08 (3.36 at next open). Microsoft just over 3.0, Monolithic Power 2.94, Meta 2.71, KLA 2.70, Marvell 2.49 on 216 trades. Weak: Palantir, Fang, Airbnb, CrowdStrike.
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: Same family as the RSI(2) sweep, but across single stocks rather than an index, with a different oscillator.
ideas.red_flags: Survivorship and selection bias, stated by the video: today's constituents tested backwards. The 101 stocks share market days, so 95 of 101 is not 95 independent confirmations. Costs and period unstated. Short-history names have few trades. We would need a current constituent list; point-in-time membership is not free. Headline names are the best of 101, so the median is the number to trust.
ideas.why_priority: Breadth across 101 names is a far stronger luck test than another SPY run, rules are complete, and the median profit factor is a clear number to check.

ideas.title: I Backtested 10 Oscillators on SPY for 33 Years
ideas.name: Williams %R(7) below -95 on SPY, frozen development and holdout (also FXYI7n6XJlk)
ideas.entry: Williams %R over 7 days is below -95 at the daily close; buy SPY at the next open; one position at a time.
ideas.exit: SPY closes above the previous day's high; exit at the next open. The video also tests fixed 1, 3 and 5 day exits.
ideas.claimed_results: 1993 to 2026: 288 trades, profit factor 2.61, average trade 0.82%, 76.4% winners, max drawdown 12.1%. Profit factor by era: 3.01 (1993-2003), 2.51 (2004-2014), 2.28 (2015-2026). Second video: 42 parameter combinations, settings chosen on 1993-2015 and locked, untouched 2016-2026 holdout profit factor 2.08 (RSI 1.12, stochastic 1.75). Median profit factor across the 42 development combinations 2.02. Scorecard 92 out of 100 against 75 and 33. Costs excluded.
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: Same entry style and the same close-above-yesterday's-high exit as the RSI(2) sweep, which was not among the P-0082 survivors. Likely trades many of the same days as the RSI(5) book.
ideas.red_flags: Winner of a 10-way contest and of a 42-combination grid, so selection bias. The holdout is not clean: the three oscillators compared in the second video were shortlisted from the earlier full-sample ranking. Williams %R(7) below -95 is just the close sitting in the bottom 5% of the 7-day range, a fast stochastic. Costs excluded. Ten oscillators with one exit are largely one trade, not ten edges.
ideas.why_priority: Complete rules and a stated holdout number to check, but it is a close relative of something we already tested, so run it with the permutation test and measure entry-day overlap with the RSI(5) book.

ideas.title: This Stochastic Strategy Won 77.7% Over 33 Years
ideas.name: 7-day slow stochastic below 25 on SPY
ideas.entry: 7-day stochastic with 3-bar smoothing (slow %K) closes below 25. Headline test buys at that same close; realistic variant buys at the next open.
ideas.exit: Sell when price closes above yesterday's high (at that close; next open in the variant). No stop, no target, never more than one position.
ideas.claimed_results: 33 years of SPY. Close entry: 394 trades, 77.7% winners, profit factor 2.58, average trade 0.68% before costs. Next-open entry and exit: 394 trades, 73.6% winners, profit factor 2.47, average 0.65%. Lookbacks 4 to 12 all profitable with profit factor above 2.2. Alternative exits (stochastic above 50, 60 or 70; fixed 3 or 5 days) all profitable. Three eras: profit factor 2.66, 2.76, 2.23; last era 107 trades, 75.7% winners. Companion video: holdout 2016-2026 profit factor 1.75, median development grid profit factor 2.41. The oscillator-ranking video quotes 393 trades and 2.48 for the same setup.
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: Same family as the RSI(2) sweep (same exit); likely overlaps RSI(5) days.
ideas.red_flags: One market, in-sample, before commissions and slippage (the video says so). Close-entry headline is not executable exactly. Later era is weaker and holdout drops to 1.75. Shares an exit with every other idea in this family.
ideas.why_priority: Complete rules, a stated next-open result and parameter neighbourhood to reproduce; run in the same batch as A-03 because they are one family.

ideas.title: Can Mean Reversion and Trend Following Work Together?
ideas.name: Weak-Monday reversal: Monday closes below the prior Friday's low, hold to Friday (also q6aVe5uOuH4)
ideas.entry: On a Monday, the close is below the previous Friday's low. In the combined strategy this leg also requires the close to be below the 200-day average. Entry price is not spoken; the Monday close is the likely reading. The transcript of this passage is garbled.
ideas.exit: Friday's close (the transcript adds a clause about the 200-day average that does not parse).
ideas.filters: close below 200-day average in the UYI0 version; none in the q6aVe5uOuH4 version
ideas.claimed_results: From q6aVe5uOuH4 (unfiltered, S&P 500, a strategy they sell): average gain 0.6% per trade, equal to about 7% a year, invested only 12% of the time; described as a pattern in which a weak Monday raises the odds of gains over the next four days to Friday's close. From UYI0 the bear-market leg is only quoted inside the 12% combined return (see A-14).
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: none
ideas.red_flags: Rules garbled and the sales version leaves 'weak' undefined. The numbers do not reconcile: 7% a year at 0.6% a trade is about 12 trades a year, and at a four-day hold that is about 19% exposure, not 12%, unless holds are shorter. No trade count, period or costs. Calendar effects are easy to overfit and the same channel found the Monday open-to-close effect to be noise (A-33).
ideas.why_priority: Cheap daily-only test of a calendar and reversal idea nothing in our set resembles, with a stated result, though the rule needs two readings pre-registered.

ideas.title: AI Created a Profitable SPY Strategy. Then We Tried to Break It
ideas.name: SPY above 200-day average, RSI(3) below 20, dip-buy
ideas.entry: SPY close above its 200-day average and RSI(3) below 20 at the close; buy by the next open. RSI smoothing type (Wilder or other) unstated.
ideas.exit: Exit 'after a rebound' with the exact rule unstated. Alternative fixed exits tested: 1, 3, 5, 10 and 21 days.
ideas.claimed_results: Start 1993. 253 trades, 75.9% winners, profit factor 2.60, average trade 0.60%; $10,000 grew to about $44,000. 1993-2014 profit factor 2.93; 2015 onward 2.18 on 104 trades. All 20 nearby RSI-length and threshold combinations profitable. Trend filter 150 to 250 days: full-sample profit factor 2.58 to 2.73, later period above 2. Every alternative exit profitable. Costs: 10 basis points round trip gives 2.25, 20 gives 1.94. Weakest of four eras: 2010-2019 at 1.85. My arithmetic: $10,000 to $44,000 over about 33 years is roughly 4.6% a year.
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: Close relative of the running RSI(5) book (RSI dip-buy with a 200-day filter) and of the RSI(2) sweep.
ideas.red_flags: Exit rule not stated, so the headline cannot be reproduced exactly. The video is honest about later weakness. The compounding figure is low in absolute terms because exposure is low. Frames itself as AI-found in 30 seconds, which is theatre.
ideas.why_priority: Good robustness numbers, but it is the closest thing to our current book and the exit is missing.

ideas.title: I Backtested 10 Oscillators on SPY for 33 Years
ideas.name: 7-day Chande Momentum Oscillator below -60 on SPY
ideas.entry: CMO over 7 days below -60 at the daily close; buy at the next open.
ideas.exit: Close above the previous day's high; exit at the next open.
ideas.claimed_results: 219 trades, profit factor 2.42, average trade 0.70%. Ranked fifth of ten. Described as having fewer trades and more variation across eras than the leaders; no era numbers given.
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: Same family and same exit as A-03 and A-04.
ideas.red_flags: Few trades, no robustness numbers given, selected from a ten-way ranking.
ideas.why_priority: Complete rule but adds nothing the stochastic and Williams runs will not already cover.

ideas.title: Cutler's RSI: Does This Version Work Better?
ideas.name: RSI(3) below 10 on QQQ, Wilder smoothing against Cutler (simple average) smoothing
ideas.entry: 3-day RSI closes below 10; buy at the next open. Run once with Wilder RSI and once with Cutler RSI (simple average of gains and losses).
ideas.exit: Sell when the close finishes above yesterday's high (limit on close). Long only, no stop.
ideas.claimed_results: Period unstated. Wilder RSI(3): 128 trades. Cutler RSI(3): 434 trades, bigger and longer drawdowns, higher total profit, strategy return 13.5% a year against 10.8% for buy and hold, exposure about four times the Wilder version. After equalising trade counts the author says Cutler looks better, with no numbers. Comparison table was on screen, not spoken. Commission and slippage assumed near zero.
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: Partly: RSI(2) sweep and the RSI(5) book use Wilder-style RSI on short lookbacks.
ideas.red_flags: Few numbers spoken. The 10.8% buy-and-hold figure is also quoted for SPY in UYI0piMbq2Q, so one of the two is misattributed or the periods differ. The author's preferred comparison is a re-tuned one with no results shown.
ideas.why_priority: Cheap and useful as an implementation check: at short lookbacks RSI definition changes trade count threefold, which matters for our RSI(5) book.

ideas.title: Every Popular Trading Strategy Explained in 14 Minutes (Backtested)
ideas.name: RSI(2) below 10 in, RSI(2) above 70 out on QQQ
ideas.entry: 2-day RSI drops below 10; entry price unstated.
ideas.exit: 2-day RSI rises above 70.
ideas.claimed_results: Average gain per trade almost 1%; invested about 22% of the time; tracked buy and hold with lower drawdowns. No period, trade count, win rate or profit factor.
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: RSI(2) threshold sweep, but with a different exit (RSI above 70 rather than close above yesterday's high) and on QQQ.
ideas.red_flags: No trade count or period. The sister video with the other exit quotes the same near-1% average with 12% exposure, so exposure is inconsistent between exits.
ideas.why_priority: A complete rule on a different exit and market, but the claim is too thin to check.

ideas.title: This EURO STOXX 50 Strategy Had a 75.6% Win Rate
ideas.name: Euro Stoxx 50 low-volatility pullback inside an uptrend
ideas.entry: All three on the signal day: 14-day ATR is within the lowest 25% of its readings over the previous year (relative or absolute ATR unstated); close below the 20-day average; close above the 200-day average. Buy at the next session's open.
ideas.exit: unstated; withheld for paying members. The video only says several exits worked reasonably.
ideas.filters: 200-day average trend filter, low-ATR volatility filter
ideas.claimed_results: Backtest from 1999, coded in TradeStation. 119 trades (about 4 a year, my arithmetic), about 75% winners (title says 75.6%), profit factor 2.83, average profit $259 per contract per trade. Before commissions and slippage.
ideas.data_needed_if_not: True futures P&L per contract needs FESX contract data and costs. The cash index (Yahoo ^STOXX50E, history probably from 2007, to verify) or a continuous future is a usable proxy, and we would pick our own exit.
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: Pullback-in-uptrend logic overlaps the RSI(5) book, but the low-ATR filter, the non-US market and the index-futures setting are new.
ideas.red_flags: The exit, the part that decides a mean-reversion result, is behind a paywall. Costs excluded, which the video admits. A short free history means a fraction of the 119 trades. Funnel.
ideas.why_priority: The low-volatility filter is worth testing as an add-on to the RSI(5) entries, but the result cannot be checked without the exit.

ideas.title: Do Simple Market Timing Rules Actually Work?
ideas.name: 75-day Donchian close breakout on SPY, TLT and GLD, one-third each
ideas.entry: For each asset separately, go long when the close breaks above the highest close of the last 75 days. Execution timing unstated.
ideas.exit: Sell when the close breaks below the lowest close of the last 75 days.
ideas.sizing: 33% of capital to each asset; unused slots stay in cash
ideas.claimed_results: No figures spoken. Described as a fairly steady upward curve, rough around 2008 and 2021-2023 but recovering to new highs, with a decent CAGR and very low drawdown, returns arriving in clusters, partly in cash. Period unstated.
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: Partly: P-0084 is a 28-market trend portfolio; this is a three-asset special case with a Donchian rule and fixed one-third sizing.
ideas.red_flags: No numbers to check. GLD history starts late 2004. Three assets only.
ideas.why_priority: Complete rule but no stated result, and it can ride along inside P-0084 at almost no cost.

ideas.title: Do Simple Market Timing Rules Actually Work?
ideas.name: Fabian timing model: three indices above the 39-week average
ideas.markets: SPY, confirmed by the S&P 500, the Dow Jones Industrial Average and a utilities index
ideas.entry: Long SPY when all three indices are above their 39-week moving average.
ideas.exit: Sell when at least two of the three break below the 39-week average. What the capital does afterwards is unstated, presumably cash.
ideas.claimed_results: No figures spoken. Said to have avoided the worst drawdowns, beaten buy and hold despite not being fully invested, and cut drawdowns significantly. Period unstated.
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: Same family as the 200 versus 222-day average filter test on SPY.
ideas.red_flags: No numbers. Which utilities index is unstated (Yahoo may offer ^DJU; XLU is a shorter proxy, to verify). Very few trades, so little statistical power.
ideas.why_priority: Complete weekly rule, but no stated result and few signals.

ideas.title: We Backtested Global Equities Momentum Across 55 Years
ideas.name: Antonacci global equities momentum (US versus non-US versus bills, monthly)
ideas.markets: US equities, non-US equities, Treasury bills, US aggregate bonds
ideas.entry: At month end compute trailing 12-month returns. If US equities have not beaten Treasury bills, hold US aggregate bonds. Otherwise hold whichever of US or non-US equities has the higher 12-month return, for the next month.
ideas.exit: Implicit: switches at the next month end.
ideas.filters: absolute momentum (equities versus bills) plus relative momentum (US versus non-US)
ideas.claimed_results: From a paper by someone else, January 1971 to July 2026: 15.2% a year against 11.3% for the S&P 500; max drawdown 21.7% against 50.9%; about 1.5 position changes a year. Absolute momentum alone about 12%, relative alone about 13.3%. A static portfolio at the same average allocation made about 10%. In the 11 calendar years the S&P fell, it lost 14.4% on average and the strategy 0.4%. 2010 to 2026: about 9.5% a year against over 14%. Worst drawdown late 2021 to 2023, in bonds for 13 of 23 months.
ideas.data_needed_if_not: A 1971 start needs index and mutual-fund history we cannot get free. ETF proxies (SPY, EFA from about 2001 or ACWX from about 2008, BIL or ^IRX, AGG from about 2003; dates to verify) give about 20 years.
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: Loose overlap with P-0084 (trend and momentum portfolio).
ideas.red_flags: Third-party paper, not their own test. Has underperformed the S&P since 2010, which the video says plainly. Roughly 20 years of free ETF data is about 240 monthly decisions, too few for a strong luck test.
ideas.why_priority: Fully specified with checkable claims, but a well-known strategy with a decade-long decay and thin free data.

ideas.title: Can Mean Reversion and Trend Following Work Together?
ideas.name: 200-day trend following plus bear-market mean reversion on SPY
ideas.entry: Trend leg: buy when the close crosses above the 200-day average (next-day open is said to work equally well). Mean-reversion leg: A-05, used while SPY is below its 200-day average.
ideas.exit: Trend leg: sell when the close crosses below the 200-day average. Mean-reversion leg: A-05 exit.
ideas.filters: the 200-day average decides which leg is active
ideas.claimed_results: Period unstated. Combined about 12% a year against 10.8% for buy and hold, invested about 80% of the time. The trend leg alone did not beat buy and hold; the mean-reversion leg during bear markets provided the gain. The author calls it a simple example.
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: The trend leg is the 200-day SPY test already run in P-0082.
ideas.red_flags: Mean-reversion leg is garbled in the transcript. No period, trade count or drawdown. The 10.8% buy-and-hold figure matches the QQQ figure in eX9oMUUNgaE.
ideas.why_priority: The trend leg is already tested and the new leg is the unstated A-05, so this is only worth running after A-05.

ideas.title: Every Popular Trading Strategy Explained in 14 Minutes (Backtested)
ideas.name: 200-day average trend following on Bitcoin
ideas.entry: Buy when the close ends above the 200-day average.
ideas.exit: Sell when the close ends below it.
ideas.claimed_results: 37 trades; the annual return figure is garbled in the transcript. Said to have worked very well. Period unstated.
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: The 200-day rule is the P-0082 SPY test, but on a different market.
ideas.red_flags: Result missing from the transcript. Bitcoin history of about a decade is one regime. Whether the video means a close-based signal with next-open entry is unstated.
ideas.why_priority: Complete and cheap, but no number to check and a short, regime-dependent history.

ideas.title: I Backtested 10 Famous Trading Rules Over 33 Years
ideas.name: Buy the dip: SPY down 5% in 5 days, buy next open, hold 5 sessions
ideas.entry: SPY has fallen at least 5% in 5 days; buy at the next open.
ideas.exit: Sell after 5 sessions.
ideas.claimed_results: 1993 to 2026, 81 cases (events are described as non-overlapping): average return +1.24% against +0.20% for a normal 5-day period.
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: Subsumed in spirit by the RSI(5) dip-buying book; this is the extreme-drop tail of the same behaviour.
ideas.red_flags: 81 cases are likely clustered in a few crashes (2008, 2020). No dispersion, worst case or costs given.
ideas.why_priority: A complete event rule that needs no parameter search, useful as a control for the dip-buying book.

ideas.title: I Backtested 10 Famous Trading Rules Over 33 Years
ideas.name: Sell the rip: SPY up 5% in 5 days, then weaker next 5 days
ideas.entry: Event: SPY has gained at least 5% in 5 days. Observed over the following 5 days. Whether to short or merely skip long entries is not stated.
ideas.exit: Measured after 5 days.
ideas.claimed_results: 1993 to 2026: next-5-day average -0.24% against a normal +0.20%; 53.9% of cases positive, so the negative average comes from the size of the losing episodes. Number of events not given.
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: none
ideas.red_flags: Sample size unstated and probably small. Long-only systems cannot short it, so its use would be as an entry filter.
ideas.why_priority: Cheap event study that could serve as a skip-entry filter, but small sample and no trade rule.

ideas.title: This Simple Triple RSI Strategy Won 88.9% of Its Trades
ideas.name: Triple RSI on SPY
ideas.entry: RSI(5) below 30; RSI has fallen for three consecutive sessions; the RSI reading three sessions earlier was below 60; SPY above its 200-day average. Buy at the close.
ideas.exit: At the close when RSI rises above 50. No stop, no target.
ideas.claimed_results: February 1993 to September 2026: 90 trades, 88.9% winners, average trade 1.25%, profit factor 5.53, average hold just under five days. Searched 11,683 configurations; among 1,125 nearby ones the median profit factor was 3.86 and 94.8% had a profit factor of at least 2. Some combinations exceeded 20 and one 30; requiring at least 100 trades removed the extremes but left several above 6. Original profit factor by era: 6.31 (1993-2002), 5.57 (2003-2012), 11.39 (2013-2022), 2.07 (2023 to September 2026). The channel plans a follow-up testing one, two and three RSI conditions.
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: High: P-0082 already tested RSI(5) simple, double and triple on SPY, and the running systems book is RSI(5) dip-buying.
ideas.red_flags: 90 trades is small; the original is the video's own warning. Trades only about three a year. The 2023-2026 drop to 2.07 is the real news. Buying at the signal close is optimistic. Costs excluded.
ideas.why_priority: Already tested; the only new datum is the post-2023 decay, which the forward paper book will show for itself.

ideas.title: Apple vs Nvidia vs Tesla: One Triple RSI Strategy, 5 Very Different Results
ideas.name: Triple RSI on five single stocks (Apple, Amazon, AMD, Nvidia, Tesla)
ideas.entry: RSI(5) below 30 and down three sessions in a row; RSI three sessions earlier below 60; the stock above its own 200-day average. Buy at the close.
ideas.exit: At the close when RSI rises above 50. No stop, no target.
ideas.claimed_results: September 2016 to September 2026. Apple: 27 trades, about 82% winners, average trade 0.90%, profit factor 2.17. Amazon: 25 trades, 72% winners, profit factor 1.70, average about 0.80%. Tesla: about 55% winners, average -0.80%, profit factor 0.83. Nvidia: 26 trades, 24 winners (92.3%), average 3.82%, profit factor 19.24. AMD: 33 trades, average 4.65%, profit factor 22.29.
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: Extends the SPY triple RSI to stocks, which we have not tested.
ideas.red_flags: Five hand-picked, famous winners over a decade; 25 to 33 trades each. The profit factors above 19 come from a handful of trades in two semiconductor names, and the video asks whether it is a semiconductor tendency or a lucky sample. Better answered on a broad universe, as in A-02.
ideas.why_priority: The question is good but five chosen stocks cannot answer it; use a wide universe instead.

ideas.title: We Backtested Connors RSI: The Results Surprised Us
ideas.name: Two-day Connors RSI below 10 on QQQ
ideas.entry: Connors RSI below 10; buy at the next open. Connors RSI is the average of a short RSI of closes, an RSI of the up or down streak, and the percent rank of the latest one-day return over about 100 days. The exact lengths are unstated.
ideas.exit: Close above yesterday's high; long only, no stop.
ideas.claimed_results: Period unstated. Average gain per trade almost 1%, win rate 70%, invested about 12% of the time; slippage and commissions not included. Better than traditional RSI(2) on profit factor and risk-adjusted return, but the differences are small. The comparison table was not spoken. On SPY, the oscillator-ranking video puts Connors RSI at profit factor 2.12 on 298 trades with a 12.4% max drawdown, eighth of ten.
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: RSI(2) sweep with the same exit.
ideas.red_flags: Which parameters are used is unstated, so it cannot be reproduced exactly. Small edge over plain RSI(2) by the author's own account. The video says RSI works worse outside stocks.
ideas.why_priority: Incomplete parameters, a marginal improvement over what we tested, and ranked low in the channel's own comparison.

ideas.title: 3 Popular Trading Indicators Tested Over 33 Years
ideas.name: Plain RSI as the baseline: RSI(7) below 30 and RSI(4) below 30 on SPY
ideas.entry: RSI(7) below 30 (FXYI7n6XJlk) or RSI(4) below 30 (zixcw9KZzp0) at the close; buy at the next open.
ideas.exit: Same exit for every oscillator; in the sister video it is close above the previous day's high, exit next open.
ideas.claimed_results: RSI(7)<30: 241 trades, profit factor 2.18 over 1993-2026, holdout 2016-2026 profit factor 1.12, median development-grid profit factor 2.21. RSI(4)<30: 465 trades, profit factor 1.99, average trade 0.51%, 71.8% winners; ranked fourth of ten.
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: Direct: RSI with the close-above-yesterday's-high exit is the RSI(2) sweep; the video's RSI(7) holdout collapse is a useful contrast with our RSI(5) survivor.
ideas.red_flags: Same shortlist-selection issue as A-03. The comparison is across oscillators, not a standalone claim.
ideas.why_priority: Already tested; its value is as the weak baseline in a head-to-head with A-03 and A-04.

ideas.title: I Backtested 10 Oscillators on SPY for 33 Years
ideas.name: Internal bar strength (IBS) dip-buy on SPY
ideas.entry: IBS below an unstated threshold at the close; buy at the next open. (IBS is where the close sits within the day's range.)
ideas.exit: Close above the previous day's high; exit next open.
ideas.claimed_results: 631 trades (the most of the ten), profit factor 2.12. Ranked sixth of ten.
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: Same family and exit as A-03.
ideas.red_flags: Threshold unstated.
ideas.why_priority: Threshold missing and ranked mid-table; a threshold sweep is easy once the family is run.

ideas.title: I Backtested 10 Famous Trading Rules Over 33 Years
ideas.name: Falling knife: SPY down 10% in 10 days, buy and hold 20 days
ideas.entry: SPY has dropped at least 10% in 10 days; buy at the next open.
ideas.exit: Sell after 20 days.
ideas.claimed_results: 1993 to 2026: 17 independent events, average return +4.27%, 76.5% positive. A normal 20-day return in the same video is +0.78%.
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: Extreme-tail version of A-16.
ideas.red_flags: 17 events, likely concentrated in a few crash episodes. The video flags the small sample itself.
ideas.why_priority: Sample too small to test; useful only as a sanity check on A-16.

ideas.title: I Backtested 10 Famous Trading Rules Over 33 Years
ideas.name: Three lower closes in a row, buy next open, hold three days
ideas.entry: Three consecutive lower closes; buy at the next open.
ideas.exit: Sell after three days.
ideas.claimed_results: 459 observations, average +0.23% against +0.12% normal over 3 days.
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: The triple RSI falls-for-three-sessions condition is a cousin.
ideas.red_flags: Very small edge per trade; costs would consume much of it.
ideas.why_priority: A big sample but an edge about 0.1 percentage points, which costs would eat.

ideas.title: I Backtested 10 Famous Trading Rules Over 33 Years
ideas.name: Sell in May: November to April versus May to October on SPY
ideas.entry: Hold November through April.
ideas.exit: Sell for May through October (what to hold instead is unstated).
ideas.claimed_results: 1993 to 2026: May to October averaged +3.34%, November to April averaged +6.07%. The summer half was still positive, so the video calls the slogan only half true.
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: none
ideas.red_flags: About 33 observations per half. Both halves positive means any rule that sits out summer gives up return.
ideas.why_priority: Well-known calendar effect with only about 33 independent years and no tradable rule given.

ideas.title: Every Popular Trading Strategy Explained in 14 Minutes (Backtested)
ideas.name: Gold breakout confirmed by another asset (their strategy number 12)
ideas.entry: Gold makes a new high and the move is confirmed by a rise in another asset (not named, window unstated).
ideas.exit: unstated
ideas.claimed_results: Since GLD began: average gain 0.35% per trade after commission and slippage, 567 trades in 20 years, 75% winners, max drawdown 13%.
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: none
ideas.red_flags: Entry confirmation, exit and period all unstated; the system is sold on their site. The only claim in the folder that says it is after costs, though the cost model is not given.
ideas.why_priority: A tempting stated result, but we would have to guess the rules.

ideas.title: Every Popular Trading Strategy Explained in 14 Minutes (Backtested)
ideas.name: Moon phases: invest around the new moon
ideas.entry: Hold during the new-moon phase; window length unstated.
ideas.exit: Leave at the end of that phase; full moon is described as bearish.
ideas.claimed_results: Said to beat buy and hold; no numbers.
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: none
ideas.red_flags: No rules or numbers. A natural cheap control experiment for the permutation machinery because the prior is near zero.
ideas.why_priority: Rules missing, but the test is trivial (moon phase is computable) and tells us how often our luck test is fooled.

ideas.title: Every Popular Trading Strategy Explained in 14 Minutes (Backtested)
ideas.name: Monthly rotation across gold, bonds, US stocks and international stocks
ideas.markets: gold, bonds, US stocks, international stocks
ideas.entry: Invest in the asset with the best recent momentum; lookback and number of assets held unstated.
ideas.exit: Rotate at the next month end.
ideas.claimed_results: Published about 10 years ago and still performing; average annual return 12.5%, drawdowns about 21%.
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: Related to A-13 and P-0084.
ideas.red_flags: Lookback unstated. Results quoted from their site without period or costs.
ideas.why_priority: Rules incomplete; A-13 is the specified version of the same idea.

ideas.title: Every Popular Trading Strategy Explained in 14 Minutes (Backtested)
ideas.name: VIX-triggered buy signals on the S&P 500
ideas.entry: A VIX condition triggers a buy; the condition is unstated.
ideas.exit: unstated
ideas.claimed_results: Published in 2020 and said to have performed better than ever since; no numbers.
ideas.data_needed_if_not: VIX daily history is free (Yahoo ^VIX); only the rules are missing.
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: none
ideas.red_flags: No rule, no number. Any VIX threshold we choose would be our own invention, so a multiple-testing trap.
ideas.why_priority: Free data but nothing to reproduce; pre-register our own small family if wanted.

ideas.title: Every Popular Trading Strategy Explained in 14 Minutes (Backtested)
ideas.name: Short the S&P 500 at the open, cover at the close
ideas.entry: Short at the open on days meeting an unstated condition.
ideas.exit: Cover at the close.
ideas.claimed_results: Trades rarely; average gain 0.3% per trade after commissions and slippage.
ideas.data_needed_if_not: Open-to-close is testable on daily bars, so no intraday data is needed; only the day condition is missing.
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: none
ideas.red_flags: Condition unstated. The same channel finds plain Monday and Friday open-to-close effects are near zero (A-33).
ideas.why_priority: Nothing to reproduce without the condition.

ideas.title: I Backtested 10 Famous Trading Rules Over 33 Years
ideas.name: Golden cross and death cross: 63-day forward returns after the 50 and 200-day cross
ideas.entry: Event: 50-day average crosses above (golden) or below (death) the 200-day average.
ideas.exit: Measured after 63 days.
ideas.claimed_results: 1993 to 2026. Golden cross: next 63 days +5.42% against +2.43% normal, 86.7% positive, 15 independent signals. Death cross: next 63 days +5.76%, 80% positive; the bearish signal failed in this sample.
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: High: Davey's golden cross was tested in P-0082.
ideas.red_flags: 15 signals; death cross sample not stated.
ideas.why_priority: Already tested and the sample is about 15 events.

ideas.title: I Backtested 10 Famous Trading Rules Over 33 Years
ideas.name: Buy new highs: close at a 252-day high on SPY
ideas.entry: Event: close at a 252-day high.
ideas.exit: Measured after 20 days.
ideas.claimed_results: Next 20 days averaged +0.42% against +0.78% normal, though 71.4% were positive.
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: none, but it is a negative result for a momentum idea.
ideas.red_flags: Only useful as a warning that buying strength on SPY at this horizon underperforms.
ideas.why_priority: A negative result; nothing to trade.

ideas.title: I Backtested 10 Famous Trading Rules Over 33 Years
ideas.name: Monday effect: Monday and Friday open-to-close returns on SPY
ideas.entry: Buy the Monday open (or short the Friday open).
ideas.exit: Same-day close.
ideas.claimed_results: 1,587 Monday observations: average +0.018% open to close; Friday average -0.013%. Judged noise.
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: none
ideas.red_flags: Nothing to trade.
ideas.why_priority: Reported as noise.

ideas.title: I Backtested 10 Famous Trading Rules Over 33 Years
ideas.name: The trend is your friend: forward 20 days when SPY is above its 200-day average
ideas.entry: Event: close above the 200-day average.
ideas.exit: Measured after 20 days.
ideas.claimed_results: Next 20 days averaged +0.88% against +0.78% normal. Derived, not stated: since the unconditional figure is 0.78%, days below the 200-day average must average lower; the video does not report them.
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: High: the 200-day test in P-0082.
ideas.red_flags: Tiny difference above the average; the filter's worth is on the below side, which is not shown.
ideas.why_priority: Already tested in P-0082.

ideas.title: Do Simple Market Timing Rules Actually Work?
ideas.name: Coppock Curve on monthly S&P 500
ideas.entry: Long when the Coppock Curve (10-month weighted moving average of the sum of the 14-month and 11-month rate of change) crosses above zero.
ideas.exit: Sell when it breaks below zero.
ideas.claimed_results: From 1960, 13 trades returned 6.5% (basis unstated, likely a yearly rate), invested 73% of the time. Avoided the worst drawdowns but did not beat buy and hold.
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: Loose overlap with the 200-day trend tests.
ideas.red_flags: 13 trades; admitted not to beat buy and hold.
ideas.why_priority: Thirteen trades and no edge over buy and hold.

ideas.title: I Backtested 10 Oscillators on SPY for 33 Years
ideas.name: Stochastic RSI, CCI, Connors RSI and Ultimate Oscillator dip-buys on SPY
ideas.entry: Oversold signal from each oscillator at the close, buy at the next open; thresholds and lengths unstated.
ideas.exit: Close above the previous day's high; exit next open.
ideas.claimed_results: Stochastic RSI profit factor 1.81 on 488 trades; CCI 1.97 on 285; Connors RSI 2.12 on 298 with 12.4% max drawdown; Ultimate Oscillator 1.96 on 479. All four finished in the bottom half of ten.
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: Same family as A-03.
ideas.red_flags: No parameters given.
ideas.why_priority: Bottom-ranked in the video's own comparison with no parameters.

ideas.title: I Backtested 10 Oscillators on SPY for 33 Years
ideas.name: QSRSI, the channel's own RSI-based oscillator
ideas.entry: Oversold QSRSI at the close, buy at the next open; formula and threshold unstated.
ideas.exit: Close above the previous day's high; exit next open.
ideas.claimed_results: Profit factor 2.63 on 271 trades, average trade 0.84%, 76.8% winners; finished second overall after robustness checks, slightly above the winner's 2.61 headline.
ideas.data_needed_if_not: The QSRSI formula, which the video does not give.
ideas.overlaps_what_we_have: Closest to our RSI(5) work, but unknowable.
ideas.red_flags: A proprietary indicator presented in a ranking it won second place in, with no formula.
ideas.why_priority: Cannot be coded.

frameworks.name: Frozen development and holdout with an equal parameter budget
frameworks.what_it_is: Give each candidate the same number of parameter combinations (42 each), choose settings on 1993 to 2015, lock them, then judge only on an untouched 2016 to 2026 holdout. Use one common exit for all, switch no rules after seeing results, report the median profit factor over the whole grid as well as the winner, and score on fixed categories (profit factor, average trade, parameter robustness, drawdown, time robustness, trade count).
frameworks.how_proteus_could_use_it: A template for pre-registering the week-8 review: same parameter budget per idea, a locked development window, a holdout nobody touches, and the grid median as a second pass mark beside the winner. Beware the lesson from this folder: a shortlist chosen from full-sample results contaminates the holdout.

frameworks.name: Neighbourhood robustness battery
frameworks.what_it_is: Do not trust the best cell. Sweep the main parameters, report the share of nearby settings with profit factor at least 2 and the median, require at least 100 trades before ranking, and keep the original pre-search rule rather than swapping in the search winner. Add: swap the exit across fixed 1, 3, 5, 10 and 21 day exits, split into eras, delay entry and exit to the next open, and stress costs at 10 and 20 basis points round trip (5yq3TpRpzuM and 7RUVOGEtAe0 run the same battery).
frameworks.how_proteus_could_use_it: Add 'share of neighbours passing' and a cost-stress column to the systems book and to bin/review.py as a companion to the permutation test, which answers a different question (luck versus structure).

frameworks.name: Event study against same-horizon unconditional drift
frameworks.what_it_is: Turn a slogan into one frozen definition, use non-overlapping events, execute at the next open, and compare the conditional forward return with SPY's normal return over the same horizon, always quoting event count.
frameworks.how_proteus_could_use_it: Run a drift-adjusted baseline for every new entry rule, including 'same exit from random entry days', so that exit-driven win rates are separated from entry edge. The close-above-yesterday's-high exit shared by most of these ideas needs exactly that control.

frameworks.name: Breadth over best-of: report the distribution across a universe
frameworks.what_it_is: Run one frozen rule across 101 stocks and report how many pass thresholds (above 1, above 1.5, above 2) and the median, rather than the top name, and re-run with next-open entry to show the realism cost.
frameworks.how_proteus_could_use_it: Use the pass-share and median as the primary statistic for single-stock versions of the dip-buy, with a survivorship caveat written next to it.

frameworks.name: Layer low-exposure strategies and report exposure
frameworks.what_it_is: Dip-buying systems sit in the market about 12% of the time, leaving capital idle, so the proposal is to stack uncorrelated edges (trend, seasonal, other mean reversion). The combo video (UYI0piMbq2Q) shows a trend leg and a bear-market reversion leg switched by the 200-day average.
frameworks.how_proteus_could_use_it: Add an exposure percentage and a daily-P&L correlation matrix to the systems book so overlapping oscillator variants (A-03, A-04, A-07, A-22) are recognised as one edge, not four.
